description: This module is a scalable JSON parsing system implemented in Go. It processes structured and semi-structured JSON inputs, supporting standard JSON (objects/arrays), NDJSON, and multi-layer nested data. It includes dynamic schema inference, recursive normalization, nested table handling, NDJSON parsing, S3 streaming I/O, and upload workflows. Large files (>10 GB for testing; in production, typically 500MB) are routed toward a Parquet conversion pipeline (currently stubbed).

The Controller function chooses between JSON-normalization mode and Parquet mode based on file size. Files ≥10 GB are routed to Parquet conversion; smaller files are fully normalized into a custom line-delimited JSON format and uploaded to S3.

description: The parser uses explicit Schema and Column structures to represent normalized tables. Nested tables are supported via recursive `Schema` references. Rows are represented as a two-dimensional slice: each row is a slice of arbitrary values, including potentially nested subtables.

codeSnippet.name: go

description: `inferType` inspects Go values dynamically and maps them into normalized types. Composite objects (maps and arrays) are treated as `table` and recursively expanded by `normalizeJSON`.

codeSnippet.name: go

description: `normalizeJSON` converts any JSON structure (object, array, scalar) into a tabular representation. It grows the schema dynamically, supports recursive nested subtables, and produces a Row structure matching the finalized column ordering. Depth information is printed for debugging.

codeSnippet.name: go

description: `parseNDJSON` reads the file line by line and treats each line as a standalone JSON object. It integrates each object into the shared schema and performs recursive normalization for nested structures via `normalizeJSON`. NDJSON rows are appended into a common Row collection.

codeSnippet.name: go

`detectJSONType` determines whether the data is array JSON, object JSON, or NDJSON by inspecting the first byte and the presence of `}
{` patterns.

description: `ParseJsonToJson` streams the input from S3 in 5 MB chunks, reconstructs the full file, detects JSON type, normalizes the data into tabular form, and uploads it to a signed S3 URL using a custom `.tarrajson` output format. Rows are line-numbered and newline-delimited for efficient streaming and partial reads.
